Hi all — dumping the technical checklist here so Acme's ops team can paste rules directly into their firewall change request. Marked mandatory vs optional.

MANDATORY (control plane connectivity):
- TCP 443 outbound to control-plane endpoints (TLS) — Goal: restrict to these egress IPs (we will provide exact list and weekly rotation schedule). Hostname: control-api.prod.redwood-inference.com (we validate via SNI).
- UDP 53 (or TCP 53 for large responses) to your configured resolver — DNS must be allowed so the instance can resolve control-plane hostnames. If your environment restricts DNS, allow queries to the resolver IPs our instances use.
- UDP 123 (NTP) outbound to your internal NTP or to a sanctioned public NTP pool — time sync is required for mTLS validity checks.
- HTTP(S) egress to OCSP/CRL endpoints — Some CA providers perform OCSP over HTTP (80) for cert validation; allow outbound TCP 80/443 to the CA domains we list.

OPTIONAL (depends on deployment choices):
- TCP 443 to model artifact registries (if you enable remote model pulls) — we can provide separate IPs/CIDRs for artifact fetch to reduce scope.
- TCP 443 for metrics/telemetry push endpoints — if you prefer to host metrics behind your own sink, this can be disabled.

NOTES / BEHAVIORAL REQUIREMENTS:
- We strongly recommend SNAT-ing outbound traffic from the private endpoint through a small set of static egress IPs (per region). This makes firewall allowlisting straightforward and avoids per-instance variance.
- Long-lived connections: control-plane may open long-lived TLS streams (heartbeat/async events). Make sure stateful inspection timeouts are sufficient (> 20 minutes) or use connection tracking based on sockets rather than ephemeral timeouts.
- SNI is used for routing; if you implement TLS interception or SNI stripping at your egress proxy, ensure the TLS handshake reaches Redwood unmodified.
- If your proxy does TLS termination (i.e., you perform a man-in-the-middle), we require mutual TLS or a proxy configuration that preserves client certs.
- IP rotation cadence: we operate on a 7-21 day rotation window for scaling events. We'll publish changes to the CSV and provide a bulletin 72 hours before a change.

ATTACHMENT: control-plane-ip-list.csv (this is the authoritative list for the next 14 days).

If you want, we can provide a minimal iptables/nftables snippet as a starting point for your change request.

- Dev

Quick NAT and ops notes from my side:

1) Dedicated egress NAT gateway:
- Best practice is a dedicated NAT gateway (or small fleet with failover) used only for Redwood control-plane traffic. Assign static elastic IP(s) to that gateway and use SNAT so all control-plane flows egress from the same IP set.
- If you use autoscaling NAT instances, make sure the pool's public IPs are consistent with the whitelist.

2) Preserve source port for long-lived connections where possible. Some stateful firewalls rewrite ports which leads to connection resets visible on our side.

3) Idle/keepalive behavior:
- Our agents send periodic heartbeats every ~60s; set TCP idle timeouts > 120s to avoid premature teardown.

4) Proxying behaviour:
- Transparent proxies that intercept TLS break mutual authentication; if you must use a proxy, configure it in a pass-through mode for Redwood TLS endpoints or terminate with a cert we trust and present client certs upstream.

5) Failover and fallback:
- If your primary egress path is unavailable, traffic may failover to an alternative egress IP we publish. We cannot guarantee connection preservation across NAT translations during failover — expect reconnections.

I'll also add a short iptables template to the shared Drive folder.

-- Vivek
